reviews.text:
They have a phone number you can call; they answer politely and explain everything perfectly. If you need something they have, they'll tell you prices and anything else you need to know. While you're in the store, they'll offer you the products you need and give you the price without any fuss. If you don't buy it, that's fine.

The only downside is that it's on the third floor, and climbing a lot of stairs is really tiring, but it's worth it. It's quite hidden since it's inside a building with other shops; it's on the top floor. You can call ahead so they can find you when you get there. I was very happy with their service and the products.
Excellent place, very well-stocked and inexpensive, good supplies

It took me a while to find the place; I even thought it was gone, but no, all you have to do is look for the stairs leading to several apartments—it's right there. As for the service, the prices, and everything else I can think of, it's absolutely perfect.

It saddened me to see how neglected the leopard geckos are. There was so much excrement in the container. I asked about the birth date and morph of one of them, and the two people working there didn't know.

I'm only posting this because they almost sold me an animal that would have died in my care. They tried to sell me a 90-KILO tortoise.

I already had an albino hedgehog. I saw albino hedgehogs in their photos and I know you have to wait 3 to 12 months to get one.

I also saw comments saying they explain things and help people.

And I saw photos of what I wanted: Greek, Russian, and Hermann's tortoises.

I arrived prepared, with the names, photos of my space, and looking for recommendations, after walking 5 km. Three employees ignored me. Finally, I asked one if she could help me. I didn't know what those tortoises were. The three most common species of land tortoise in the world.

Honestly, I was already expecting them to tell me I had to wait months. I told her so, and I had no problem with that. But she just kept trying to sell me a sulcata tortoise. If I hadn't done my research beforehand, I would have bought it right there without knowing they can weigh up to 90 kg.

I wanted a Greek, Russian, or Hermann's tortoise, and any of those would fit in my space. I mentioned that I'd seen those and other exotic animals in their photos. They accused me of lying: "Where did you see them?" On their Google page. So what?

The reviews said they help with recommendations. The recommendation was to buy a 100 kg tortoise that would die if I bought it, because where I live there isn't enough food or space for it.

The owner or manager finally realized what was happening and called me over. I tried to explain, but she interrupted me while she was selling something to someone else. The other employee did nothing. I left.

Do you want a 100 kg tortoise? This is the place for you. Do you want one of the animals in their photos? Then this isn't the place.

I've been buying live food for my snakes from them for years... I've noticed that they change their bank account for transfers on several occasions. It's happened before that they've changed accounts, and if you don't ask them every time, you never even realize it. The bank usually just bounced the payment, but this time the transfer went through to an account they no longer use. They washed their hands of it, saying it's my bank's problem, and offered no solution. What I don't understand is why the payment went through if they no longer have that account (logically, it should have bounced). They ignored my message and aren't taking responsibility. Now I'm out of money and out of food.

You agree to the purchase with them, ask about shipping, reach an agreement, but they don't honor it, refuse to refund, and claim it's not their policy, even though you asked beforehand. When you pointed out that you had already asked, and that something was agreed upon, they just laugh and say someone else helped you, and refuse to refund your money or reach an agreement. Beware if you're thinking of buying from them.

They clearly know a lot about what they sell and the service they offer.

Hello, yesterday I bought several products for my snake, including an Exo Terra light bulb for $230 pesos. When I plugged it in, it only stayed on for 4 minutes. When I called to report this problem, they told me the product wasn't under warranty, and the salesperson said it happened due to humidity, which I understand since it's an electrical product. The store is nice, and the quality of their animals is good; it's just important that they have better customer service and can provide a proper solution instead of a knee-jerk response.

They have a lot of things, but I've bought rats as pets twice, and for some reason, they're always sick. I've bought them from other places, and they live until they're old, but for some reason, the ones here all come with some kind of bacteria in their lungs and die within months, or at most a year. When I went to complain about one that was already my companion and wanted a medical evaluation, they replied, "Oh, well, we'll exchange her for you." And when I said no, they responded very rudely, like, "Well, if not, give her citrus water and see how she does" (rats are allergic to citrus). Even so, it's a very complete place in other respects. They just need to take better care of their rodents and improve their customer service.
